question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=\operatorname{log}⁡(4x+6)$ at the point $(1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the slope of the tangent line. The slope is equal to the derivative of the curve at the given point:

$$
m=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=1}
$$

To compute $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we first express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=\operatorname{log}⁡(u),\,u=4x+6.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}\cdot 4 \\  & =\frac{4}{(4x+6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)} \\  & =\frac{2}{(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}{|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{(2(1)+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)} \\  & =\frac{2}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we know that the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,1)$ is $m=\frac{2}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}.$ Finally, we find the equation of the tangent line at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{2}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}(x-1) \\ y & =\frac{2x}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}-\frac{2}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡10}+1.\end{aligned}
$$
